item.title: Southwest to Open Premium Airport Lounges Across the Country
item.description: The airline said that lounges in Baltimore, Honolulu, Nashville and Austin, Texas, would debut starting late next year, and that seven more were in the works.
item.dc:creator: Christine Chung and Niraj Chokshi
item.media:description: Austin-Bergstrom International Airport, in Texas, is one of four airports that could be getting a Southwest Airlines premium lounge starting late next year.

item.title: Trump’s Tactics to Lower Beef Prices and Appease Ranchers Fall Short
item.description: The Agriculture Department offered new initiatives for ranchers after President Trump said he would import more beef. The moves aren’t a quick fix.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Draper
item.media:credit: Will Warasila for The New York Times
item.media:description: The U.S. cattle supply is at its smallest level since 1951.

item.title: Chevron Expansion in Venezuela Extends U.S. Influence Over Oil Riches
item.description: The U.S. energy giant, which stayed in the country after other Western companies left, will invest $7 billion in the country to more than double its production there.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott
item.category: North American Blue Energy Partners Inc
item.media:description: Oil infrastructure in Cabimas, Venezuela. Chevron’s expansion is separate from President Trump’s deal for control of oil reserves in the country.

item.title: Investors Still on Edge Over War, Debt and Inflation
item.description: U.S. and Iranian forces traded attacks again, pushing oil prices higher, stocks lower and making bond investors nervous.
item.dc:creator: Jason Karaian
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)

item.title: Employer Health Costs Are Expected to Spike in 2027
item.description: A new U.S. survey anticipates an average increase of 11 percent unless benefits are cut, the highest rate in decades. Other findings also predict a sharp rise.
item.dc:creator: Reed Abelson
item.media:credit: Morgan Lieberman for The New York Times
item.media:description: U.S. employers are bracing for what looks to be the sharpest increase in health care costs in more than two decades.

item.title: Global Bond Rates Are Rising. What Should You Do Now?
item.description: If you own bonds, they may be in a broad fund that hasn’t lost much money. And that fund may do much better in the next several years.
item.dc:creator: Ron Lieber and Tara Siegel Bernard
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)

item.title: FiveThirtyEight’s Podcast Hosts Reunite for a New Show
item.description: Nate Silver, Clare Malone and Galen Druke will host “Still Counting,” a nonpartisan politics show — on a decidedly partisan podcast network.
item.dc:creator: Katie Robertson
item.media:description: Galen Druke, left, Clare Malone and Nate Silver are hoping to resurrect the spirt of their former podcast at Crooked Media.

item.title: Saturday Evening Post Will Stop Printing After 205 Years
item.description: The magazine, famous for publishing Jack London stories and Norman Rockwell art, will continue online.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Mullin
item.media:description: The Saturday Evening Post cover from May 29, 1943.

item.title: Get to Know Your Phone’s Built-In Emergency Kit
item.description: In times of natural disasters and other dangers, special features tucked away on your iPhone or Android device could help make a difference.
item.dc:creator: J. D. Biersdorfer
item.media:description: Apple’s more recent iPhone models include the ability to communicate with emergency services by text chat over a satellite connection, as well as a demonstration mode.

item.title: Inside the Fight Against a Flesh-Eating Fly in Mexico
item.description: For the first time in a year, the U.S.-Mexico border partly reopened to cattle imports following a screwworm infestation across the region. The battle against the flesh-eating fly has only just begun deep in Mexico.
item.dc:creator: James Wagner and Luis Antonio Rojas
item.media:credit: Luis Antonio Rojas for The New York Times
item.media:description: New World screwworm flies in a cage at a facility in Metapa, Mexico, that that produces sterile flies, which when released into the wild slowly reduce the population size.

item.title: Missouri Voters Appear to Recall City Councilman Over Data Center Support
item.description: Initial results showed that residents of Independence, Mo., voted overwhelmingly to recall an official who backed billions of dollars in tax breaks for a data center.
item.dc:creator: David McCabe and Lauren McCarthy
item.media:credit: Clayton Steward for The New York Times
item.media:description: Organizers of the recall vote said the councilman, John Perkins, had failed to engage the public while the city negotiated with the developer of a data center project.

item.title: Bill Simmons’s Co-Hosts Are Tired of His A.I. Antics
item.description: The founder of The Ringer is taking flak for using artificial intelligence to conjure opinions from the deceased film critic Roger Ebert. Ads from OpenAI have recently run on the show.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Mullin
item.media:credit: Mike Windle/Getty Images for Vanity Fair
item.media:description: Film buffs are complaining that the podcast host Bill Simmons used artificial intelligence to approximate the opinions of the critic Roger Ebert, who died in 2013.

item.title: What to Know About Venezuelan Energy Following Trump’s Oil Deal
item.description: The Trump administration’s deal with a private oil company to increase oil production in the South American country could take many years to come to fruition.
item.dc:creator: Aruni Soni and Lazaro Gamio

item.title: Two More Oil Tankers Are Attacked in the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: The ships were hit near Oman on Monday, the latest attacks on vessels in the Persian Gulf. Oil prices rose more than 2 percent.
item.dc:creator: Jenny Gross
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: Vessels near the Strait of Hormuz as seen from Musandam, Oman, last week. Shipping in the strait has been mostly at a standstill, with only five ships passing through on Monday.

item.title: At G20 Meeting, Scott Bessent Accuses China of Flooding the World With Cheap Exports
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent accused China for flooding the world with its cheap exports.
item.dc:creator: Alan Rappeport and Jim Tankersley
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke at an event on Tuesday for the Group of 20 nations gathering in Asheville, N.C.

item.title: Ozempic Maker Novo Nordisk’s Investors Are Nervously Looking Into the Future
item.description: Novo Nordisk’s chief executive, Mike Doustdar, is a year into a corporate turnaround. He says investors are still underestimating the promise of the company’s drugs.
item.dc:creator: Eshe Nelson
item.media:credit: Juan Diego Reyes for The New York Times
item.media:description: Novo’s share price is languishing about 70 percent below its peak from mid-2024, when it was Europe’s most valuable public company.

item.title: Satsuki Katayama, the Woman at the Center of Japan’s Currency Fight
item.description: Japan’s finance minister, Satsuki Katayama, is under pressure to strengthen the yen while balancing competing demands from the prime minister and Washington.
item.dc:creator: River Akira Davis, Kiuko Notoya and Hisako Ueno
item.media:description: Japan’s finance minister, Satsuki Katayama, at the Tokyo Stock Exchange in January. She is seen as bridge between American and Japanese policymakers.

item.title: Bond Sell-Off Threatens to Squeeze Borrowers Around the World
item.description: Government bond yields are hitting multi-decade highs, reflecting anxiety about debt levels, deficits and inflation. The effects will extend to mortgages, business loans and other types of credit.
item.dc:creator: Eshe Nelson

item.title: How the Pentagon Is Getting Into the Venezuelan Oil Business Under Trump
item.description: The Defense Department’s Office of Strategic Capital, founded by the Biden administration to give loans to bolster the U.S. defense industry, is helping lead President Trump’s oil deal.
item.dc:creator: Edward Wong, Rebecca F. Elliott and Anatoly Kurmanaev
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
North American Blue Energy Partners Inc
item.media:credit: Adriana Loureiro Fernandez for The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump said his defense secretary and secretary of state reached an agreement with the Venezuelan government on securing billions of barrels of oil reserves “through a partnership with private business.”

item.title: Shein’s Lackluster Debut Shows a Fast-Fashion Model Left Behind
item.description: Squeezed by new trade rules, shrinking market share and labor concerns, Shein’s share decline in Hong Kong on Tuesday is a sign investors have moved on.
item.dc:creator: Sui-Lee Wee
item.media:description: A Shein display in a department store in Angers in western France in February.

item.title: Donald Trump Jr.’s Firm Leads $1 Billion Funding Round for Polymarket
item.description: The new round values the prediction market at $21 billion, up from $15 billion. Mr. Trump’s firm, 1789 Capital, will invest around $300 million.
item.dc:creator: Lauren McCarthy
item.media:description: Donald Trump Jr. with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth last year. Mr. Trump’s venture capital firm, 1789 Capital, previously invested about $200 million in Polymarket.

item.title: Expedia Fights Off Claim for Damages by Cuban Exile Families
item.description: A jury in Florida found that in their suit against the travel booking company, the plaintiffs had failed to prove ownership over tourism properties in Cuba.
item.dc:creator: David C. Adams
item.media:credit: Roberto Machado Noa/LightRocket, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Cienfuegos, Cuba, in 2019. The court found that lawyers for the plaintiffs had failed to prove ownership for Cuban properties, including one in that city.

item.title: IRS Audit Revenue Has Plummeted Under Trump, Watchdog Finds
item.description: The I.R.S. lost roughly a quarter of its employees since President Trump took office, hampering the agency’s ability to conduct audits.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Duehren
item.media:description: President Trump has moved to reduce the size of the federal work force in his second term, including at the Internal Revenue Service.

item.title: Kalshi Permanently Bars George Santos From the Platform
item.description: The prediction market said it had barred George Santos, the former congressman from New York, and fined him $71,356 over evidence he engaged in insider trading.
item.dc:creator: Lauren McCarthy
item.media:description: George Santos, the former U.S. representative from New York, in 2023.

item.title: Private Equity Wants to Invest in College Sports. Some Schools Are Wary.
item.description: As desperate as many athletic programs are for money, they are proceeding cautiously when it comes to deals with private equity.
item.dc:creator: Joe Drape
item.media:description: Private equity firms are providing a credit line of up to $30 million for each school in the Big 12 Conference, but so far no university has borrowed from it.

item.title: U.S. Start-Up and Saudi Arabia Form Data Center Partnership
item.description: Together AI, which serves open-source artificial intelligence models, announced a deal to use compute from Humain in Saudi Arabia, where it can bypass U.S. backlash over data centers.
item.dc:creator: Niko Gallogly
item.media:description: Many of Saudi Arabia’s new data centers are being built by Humain, which was started last year as part of the country’s effort to jump-start its A.I. industry and diversify its economy away from oil.

item.title: Global Oil Price Rises to $90 a Barrel After U.S. and Iran Trade Attacks
item.description: The first attacks in a month jolted energy markets. The average U.S. gasoline price remained 37 percent higher since the war began.
item.dc:creator: Jenny Gross, Jason Karaian and Rich Barbieri
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Michelle Groskopf for The New York Times

item.title: Europe Protests as U.S. Invites Russian Minister to G20 Finance Meeting
item.description: The meeting, which China and Russia are attending, is focused on the ongoing economic shock from the war in Iran, which has driven up oil prices globally.
item.dc:creator: Jim Tankersley and Alan Rappeport
item.media:description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and the Federal Reserve chairman, Kevin Warsh, in Asheville, N.C., before the summit. The International Monetary Fund has projected that global growth will slow this year and that inflation will rise.

item.title: A $480,000-a-Year Pill Reflects a New Normal for Cancer Drugs
item.description: Rasonque, the new pancreatic cancer treatment from Revolution Medicines, illustrates the huge inflation in cancer drug prices over the past two decades.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Robbins
item.category: Institute for Clinical and Economic Review
item.media:credit: Kim Raff for The New York Times
item.media:description: Daraxonrasib, a newly approved treatment for pancreatic cancer made by Revolution Medicines.

item.title: A Half-Price Luxury E.V. Comes With a Big Asterisk
item.description: The Polestar 4 is a solid car, and current incentives make it a bargain. But the company, a Chinese-owned brand, is being forced from the U.S. market.
item.dc:creator: Roy Furchgott
item.media:description: The Polestar 4, right, and Polestar 5 at a British auto show in May. The 5 will not make it to the U.S. market

item.title: Chinese Cars Could Be Huge in U.S., and That’s the Problem, Officials Say
item.description: The Times test-drove a stunning crossover from Geely that would cost under half of what its rivals charge. Two senators and many experts point to security and economic concerns as reasons for a ban.
item.dc:creator: Eric A. Taub
item.media:description: A Geely Galaxy M9 at a Chinese auto show last year. Geely, founded in China just 28 years ago, now sells almost as many vehicles worldwide as Ford.

item.title: U.A.E. To Review Banque Misr, Targeted by Iran Sanctions
item.description: The Treasury Department accused Banque Misr’s branches in the United Arab Emirates of helping Iran. The Emirati central bank promised an examination.
item.dc:creator: Vivian Nereim
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: A branch of Banque Misr in Cairo in 2024. The U.S. Treasury Department said last week that the bank was helping Iran evade sanctions.

item.description: A letter arrived in the mail from PNC Bank about an address change on a mortgage account. Was a deed theft scheme in process?
item.dc:creator: Ron Lieber

item.title: Help Wanted: ‘Forward-Deployed’ Humans for the A.I. Era
item.description: Start-ups are using the military-derived term to glorify customer-facing work as clients seek people to help set up artificial intelligence tools.
item.dc:creator: Lora Kelley

item.title: Pennsylvania Gambling Addicts Hope that ‘Skill Games’ Will Go Bust
item.description: The machines, which enjoyed legal protection until a recent court ruling, could go dark in October.

item.media:description: Despite earning about $375,000 in his best year, David Peck, who is addicted to “skill games,” has no savings.

item.title: Trump’s Venezuelan Oil Deal Relies on a Powerful and Divisive Partner
item.description: The administration will work with a private Venezuelan oil company that has close ties to the country’s government.

item.title: Treasury Bars Some Reporters From G20 Finance Meeting
item.description: Specific reporters from The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg were not granted credentials to cover the meeting of financial leaders next week in Asheville, N.C.

item.media:description: Security stopping a car outside the Omni Grove Park Inn ahead of the G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors’ meeting in Asheville, N.C.

item.title: Warsh, After Talking Tough on Inflation, Faces a ‘No-Win Situation’ on Rates
item.description: Kevin M. Warsh, the chairman of the Federal Reserve, must soon decide whether to raise interest rates if inflation does not ease, even if it draws President Trump’s ire.

item.title: 40,000 Pounds of Pabst Blue Ribbon Beer Reported Stolen in California
item.description: The company responded to the theft by setting a deadline for the return of the product. “P.S., this is real and we are deadly serious,” it said on social media.
item.dc:creator: Emmett Lindner
item.media:description: Pabst addressed the theft on Instagram: “You have exactly 18 days and 44 minutes to return our truck, no questions asked.”

item.title: Teleprompter Operator Who Bet on Trump Speeches Is Ordered to Pay Fine
item.description: Gabriel Perez had access to the president’s speeches before they were delivered and was accused of placing unlawful wagers on words that would be spoken.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang for The New York Times
item.media:description: Gabriel Perez, a former teleprompter operator for President Trump, before the start of a campaign rally in Iowa in 2024.

item.title: Thievery or Innovation? The Music Industry Grapples With A.I.
item.description: Some labels have sued A.I. music generators like Suno. Others have partnered with them. At least one has done both.
item.dc:creator: Brent Crane
item.media:credit: Matt Smith for The New York Times
item.media:description: Bill Stiteler created The Puerto Rico Song, which has been streamed on Spotify 20 million times, using the A.I. tool Suno.

item.title: As Deadly Flash Flooding Batters Nepal, Some Fear ‘the Entire Himalayas Are Melting’
item.description: A glacier unleashed a deadly flood earlier this week. For local trekking guides and climbers, the mountains were already changing.
item.dc:creator: Finn-Olaf Jones
item.media:credit: Atul Loke for The New York Times
item.media:description: Homes were heavily damaged and partially buried in thick mud and debris after a catastrophic flash flood in the Devighat area of Nuwakot district in Nepal on Wednesday.

item.title: Catastrophic Flood Exposes the Risks of Nepal’s Hydropower Bet
item.description: The loss of power-generating capacity has raised questions about an ambitious expansion of renewable energy in one of the world’s most hazard-prone mountain regions.
item.dc:creator: Alex Travelli
item.media:credit: Atul Loke for The New York Times
item.media:description: A catastrophic deluge of ice and debris knocked out over 12 percent of Nepal’s hydropower capacity within minutes, striking a heavy blow to the nation’s economic engine.

item.title: High Debt and Rising Prices Catch Up to Trump, as Midterms Near
item.description: To win in 2024, the president promised an economic course correction. Almost two years later, his agenda has made that fight even harder.
item.dc:creator: Tony Romm
item.media:description: A series of concerning economic snapshots for President Trump have been released over the past week.

item.title: “The Invisible Hand of Maria Edgeworth”: An Economist, Erased
item.description: Maria Edgeworth sneaked economic theory into her best-selling novels. Two centuries later, a new book finally gives her the credit she deserves.
item.dc:creator: Jeanna Smialek

item.title: Walmart to Pay $50 Million to Settle Opioid Lawsuit, US Says
item.description: The resolution is part of an effort to hold retailers and pharmacists accountable for what the government says were their roles in the opioid epidemic.
item.dc:creator: Ishani Desai
item.media:description: Walmart will pay $50 million to settle claims its pharmacies filled suspicious prescriptions for opioids, the Justice Department said.

item.title: Trump Says U.S. Struck Deal for Control of More Than 65 Billion Barrels of Venezuela’s Oil
item.description: The president said an agreement between the countries covered more than 65 billion barrels of reserves. A U.S. official said it would involve a partnership with a private company.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott, Simon Romero and Edward Wong
item.media:credit: Adriana Loureiro Fernandez for The New York Times
item.media:description: An oil refinery in Punto Fijo, Venezuela, in 2021. Venezuela’s president, Delcy Rodríguez, said a U.S. oil deal would have a “significant impact on our nation’s revival.”

item.title: Prediction Markets Should Be Regulated as Gambling, Appeals Court Says
item.description: The outcome contradicted an earlier appeals court decision. Federal regulators said the split rulings called for resolution by the Supreme Court.
item.dc:creator: Lauren McCarthy
item.media:credit: Eric Helgas for The New York Times
item.media:description: Prediction markets, notably Kalshi, have exploded in popularity this year.

item.title: Chevron Is in Talks to Expand in Venezuela, a Potential Win for Trump
item.description: President Trump’s administration has been pushing U.S. companies like Chevron to invest more in Venezuela’s oil industry.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca F. Elliott, Simon Romero, Anatoly Kurmanaev and Lisa Friedman
item.media:description: A Chevron-chartered oil tanker was anchored near Maracaibo, Venezuela, in February. Chevron is the only U.S. oil company with a major footprint in the country.
